findings.detail: The final answer is printed before the attempt. The attempt block, which is visible before any attempt (confirmed in Chromium and on a screenshot, outside every disclosure), ends 'Your answer should contain: A per-axis validity check, the four component equations on one t, and v = (1, 8) m/s, r = (12, 16) m at t = 4 s.' Those are exactly the two quantities the task asks the learner to find, so the reconstruction attempt can be copied. This came in with the fix round 4 rewrite of the rubric. Keep the values out of the pre-attempt criteria: 'Your answer should contain: a per-axis validity check, the four component equations on one t, and the velocity and position at t = 4 s as component pairs.' The values v = (1, 8) m/s and r = (12, 16) m belong only in the locked model response, where they already are. (Alternatively, RENDERER: render success criteria after the attempt.)

The final answer is printed before the attempt. The visible attempt block ends 'Your answer should contain: A two-column x/y setup on one clock, the position (15, 20) m at t = 5 s, and a rejected mixed-instant pair such as x(5 s) with y(4 s), (15, 16) m.' It gives the position the task asks for, and the worked rejected pair, before the learner has written anything. Use 'Your answer should contain: a two-column x/y setup on one clock, the boat's position at t = 5 s, and one pair of values you refuse to call a position, with the reason.' Keep (15, 20) m and (15, 16) m only in the locked model response.

The family closure is false for the current transfer task. It reads 'The transfer task asks you first to decide, axis by axis, whether that condition holds at all.' The linked Core2B task (Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2B-MODEL-VALIDITY-02) now states both pucks' accelerations as constant and asks whether two pucks collide. It asks for no per-axis validity decision. Use: 'Established: with both acceleration components constant, the one-dimensional relations run once per axis on a shared interval with their signs kept. The transfer task puts two bodies on one clock: a collision needs both coordinates to agree at the same t, not just the paths to cross.'

The family closure is false for the current transfer task. It reads 'The transfer task compares two equal-height events on one path using the same component facts, without solving for any time.' The linked Core2B task (Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2B-SAME-HEIGHT-VELOCITY-05) asks when the velocity points 45° below the horizontal, and solves 20 − 10t = −10 for t = 3 s. It compares no equal-height events. Use: 'Established: the apex is the event v_y = 0, with v_x unchanged and a_y = −g still acting. The transfer task names its event by a direction of motion, so the condition becomes a ratio of the two velocity components.'

The family closure misdescribes the transfer task. It says 'The transfer task asks whether the projectile model itself still holds when a force keeps acting after release.' In Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2B-PROJECTILE-VALIDITY-04, no force keeps acting on the package: the model does hold, and the decision is the package's launch velocity, taken from the plane at release. Use: '…The transfer task gives no launch velocity: you decide what the package's velocity is at the instant of release, and which forces act on it afterwards.'
